parsed.notes: No Lens B refutation found; support and quote-fidelity issues were not reviewed.

reasons: Lake identity verifies Yarborough v. Alvarado as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided 2004-06-01 with official citation 541 U.S. 652.
Lake treatment marks the authority good_law as of 2026-06-30, with a J.D.B. juvenile qualifier rather than a disclosed final overruling.
residual_risks: Currency review relies on the disclosed lake judgment fields and edges only.

reasons: Lens B does not test support fidelity; no currency defect appears from the disclosed treatment record.
The lake scope note preserves the AEDPA holding as good law while identifying the later J.D.B. juvenile qualification.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity are reserved to Lens A.
The holding should not be reused as an unqualified current juvenile-custody rule after J.D.B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the J.D.B. qualifier adjacent when this holding is surfaced as current law.

reasons: Lens B does not test the editorial home-role assignment except for currency consequences.
The authority remains SCOTUS good_law in the lake record with a disclosed J.D.B. refinement, so the Progeny / Refinement role is not refuted by treatment evidence.
residual_risks: The target home page was not among the disclosed files; this is not a Lens B defect.

reasons: The content treatment fields match the lake treatment fields: good_law, as_of_content 2004-06-01, and as_of_treatment 2026-06-30.
The lake scope note expressly accounts for J.D.B. as a juvenile qualifier and says J.D.B. distinguished Alvarado as an AEDPA-deference holding.
The disclosed negative-looking progeny edges are proposed/mentioned entries and the lake records no point_overrides.
residual_risks: The lake derivation flags audit_needed/cap_hit in some treatment lanes, but the disclosed composite judgment still states good_law.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If the renderer supports qualified badges, surface the J.D.B. juvenile qualifier near the good-law badge.

reasons: Lake identity lists court_level scotus and court U.S. Supreme Court.
A Supreme Court authority on federal Miranda/AEDPA law supports the Binding — SCOTUS weight label.
residual_risks: No jurisdiction-specific limiting field is disclosed beyond the J.D.B. juvenile qualifier.
